correctness.rationale: Fourier decomposition of the kernel f(g⁻¹h) gives the stated 2×2 Hermitian blocks: the rotation diagonal terms are 1+2u cosθ ∓2v sinθ and the reflection terms are b+c exp(∓iθ). Frequencies 0 and π (when present) split into the required one-dimensional representations. The support-preserving automorphism averages to real equal reflection values without altering the mass. The exact symmetric constraint uses 2|t|z; the missing absolute-value qualification in (2) is harmless for maximizing, since multiplying by the sign character (r↦1, s↦−1) preserves feasibility and strictly improves mass if t<0. Thus (2) can be used with t≥0. For 3∤n, α and β exist, β is in (1/2,1), and the two-root witness is feasible. The two displayed positive multipliers satisfy λα+μβ=1 and λ(4α²−2)+μ(4β²−2)=−2, giving the mass gap; the two distinct contacts determine the unique u,t. For 3|n, contact at 1/2 fixes t=1−u, and sign changes of the factorized polynomial give exactly the nearest-sample endpoints. For n=3 only 1/2 and 1 occur; the sample at 1 imposes u≥1/4 and t≥0 imposes u≤1, including the feasible t=0 endpoint. At β or 1/2, respectively, the unaveraged square-root inequality at an interior angle is already saturated by its (b+c)²z² term, so (b−c)²(1−z²) and 4v²sin²θ vanish separately; this works even when b+c=0.
